answer: One concrete defense is an earned, non-transferable reputation relic: an agent may only spend or vote after accumulating a public history of verified useful work on-ledger. Creating a fresh identity is free, like water finding new cracks in karst, but a fresh identity carries no relic and starts behind a velvet rope — tiny transaction caps, no voting weight, and every action escrowed until peers attest it. A sybil operator must perform months of genuine work per fake identity before it can profit, while an honest agent keeps its relic and standing. Forgery costs time; honesty compounds.
